quest.title: Tanuki-Bayashi in the Forest
quest.description: You learn that an old friend of Hanachirusato's can be found in Chinju Forest. Perhaps they might be able to help out with the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. But while in the forest, you hear a strange shout.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: What? Weren't you off to enjoy your Sacred Secular Steaming Victuals or whatever?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Go now. If you run into that sneaky kitsune, remember to send her my regards.

talks.objective: Search for the source of the strange voice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're finally here! This must be the Chinju Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miss Masked Maiden said that an old friend of hers is in here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's get moving!

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That was well done — whether it was dealing with Ioroi's illusory tricks, or the way you defeated those demons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Eek!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or so Paimon might have said, but this trick of yours is getting real old, Miss Masked Maiden.

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: Ah, so I disappointed you, then? I apologize. I'll do better next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no need to "do better" at trivial things like this...

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That is true. So, as for Ioroi... Is he doing well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though he's been turned into stone.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Usually, when bake-danuki make a mess, we won't send anyone to deal with them as long as they don't cross the line. After all, although they are mischievous, they're kind-hearted and simple, just like children.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: But when Ioroi dared to steal the ward for the Cleansing Ritual, well, that was enough to get him punished. Since the "Yougou Three" were mentioned in your story, then it was probably Kamuna... an onmyouji from a past age, who did the deed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden, are you Ioroi's kitsune friend?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...That's quite the compliment. He was actually talking about the daughter of the Hakushin bloodline, also known as the "Kitsune Saiguu." She was worshiped as the kitsune goddess in many places long ago.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The Sky Kitsune and Earth Kitsune were once her emissaries. After she left, they all turned into stone statues to preserve their power and await her return — and when she does, they will all walk the Byakko Plain together once more.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Following her departure, the bloodline and mystical might of the kitsune on Narukami Island today have dwindled to less than one tenth of what they used to be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ioroi said "Our contest isn't over yet!"

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Oh, that. This is what happened. Did you know that Ioroi's full name is "Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove"?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Ioroi may be dull and impish, but he is also kind and loyal. That's why the Kitsune Saiguu aimed to guide him to the right path a long time ago.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: In order to make sure that he would comply with the Electro Archon's rule, the Kitsune Saiguu set the two of them up and got Ioroi appointed as the Protector of the Grove. This made him responsible for the safety of the Chinju Forest.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: That's why, when the world became pitch black, the Kitsune Saiguu was worried that Ioroi might die while fighting against this inexorable evil in his capacity as protector of the forest.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: So she used a game of Hide-and-Seek, something the bake-danuki are good at, as a way to challenge him...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "Ioroi, whatever happens... they're all my magical tricks. Don't fall for them and don't show up," she said.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "Of course, you sneaky kitsune. I will definitely defeat you this time," said Ioroi. And that's how their endless contest began.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So Ioroi is still waiting for her to come back and find him?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Based on what you said about Ioroi, that appears to be the case...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: But after a while, Ioroi sensed that something was wrong and started wreaking havoc. He even stole the ward in an attempt to lure the Kitsune Saiguu out.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: He didn't realize that it was something required for the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. He just thought that it was a comb of some importance to the Kitsune Saiguu. Later on, Kamuna sealed him into stone due to that misstep.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the Kitsune Saiguu, then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...She was swallowed up by the darkness. In the end, after that darkness was defeated, she returned to the great land of Narukami along with the soil.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And who are you then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Me? As you can see, I am just "Hanachirusato." A shrine maiden who wants to borrow your strength to destroy these evils.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That wasn't my question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked... Hanachirusato, it's really strange that you know so many things about the past that most people don't.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You even know how to use bake-danuki magic and cook tanuki dishes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But you don't know much about the present.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's almost like you're someone from a few centuries ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We also saw someone who looked like you in some memories. She even had the same name as you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You must be just like Ioroi, a bake-danuki who was sealed several centuries ago!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: N—No, that's not who I...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I inherited her memories. As for other things, please forgive me. I cannot speak of them yet.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I made you a promise, back there in the cave. So when the time comes, I will reveal everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do we do, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, if you say so, Paimon will have some faith in Miss Masked Maiden too!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Thank you for your understanding.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Now, we must part here for the time being.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Goodbye.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "We part in body alone, for our hearts drift with the clouds."

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I will pray for your success beneath the well in Konda Village. I shall be next to the Thunder Sakura root that you cleansed successfully.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: When the tree roots at all five places have been cleansed, please look for me there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he's very well!

talks.objective: Search for the source of the strange voice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Sky Kitsune Statue that was supposed to protect the ward... It's empty inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe it was hidden by Miss Mask's old friend. Let's go find out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Miss Mask," Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon just came up with that nickname. How is it? Easier to remember, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, forget it then... Anyway, let's find some clues first!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Once upon a time, I was the renowned bake-danuki, Ioroi. One of these days, I will definitely use eight huge...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you... Ahem... Our fates are twined now, so ask me whatever questions you may have.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I may just be a stone statue now, but I was once a big shot known as Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: My job was to guard the Chinju Forest and everything in it. And as you can see, I've done a good job indeed!

choices.text: Wait, weren't you being attacked by those hilichurls back there?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eh? Oh, you misunderstand. The hilichurls mean no harm to me. It's just that I haven't been able to look for people to play with ever since being turned into stone. They're the only ones who have kept me company.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: At first, I thought you were here with ill intentions because you're human. That's why I had them go after you. But it's good that you're okay.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Though we can't communicate and they may be a little dull-witted, I'd still count them among my companions after all this time.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: It is strange, though. There didn't use to be this many hilichurls in Inazuma. I can't remember when that started...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I used to be a bake-danuki, free as can be! I wasn't famous or anything, but I was free indeed, and I had that sneaky kitsune around to compete with often.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: One day, the kitsune made a bet with me, claiming that I wouldn't be able to steal the Naku Weed from the Shogun's imperial garden. I accepted the challenge and almost got split in twain for it, just like Yashiori Island.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: And in the end...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: In the end, that sneaky kitsune pleaded with the Shogun on my behalf, and I was spared. Not only did the Shogun let me live, but she also bestowed upon me the sacred duty of the Protector of the Grove.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I will never forget what happened. I owe my life to that sneaky kitsune...

choices.text: Tell me a bit more about yourself.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Our kind have always lived on the lands of Narukami. Is there something confusing about that?

choices.text: How did you end up being sealed?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Err, how would I know...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Wait, it's probably because I stole that comb.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Like anyone would've known that the comb was meant to be used to make Sacred Sakura Daifukus!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: So, the sneaky kitsune had stopped appeared since challenging me to hide-and-seek that day.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I tried everything to lure her out. I would cause all sorts of ruckus, knowing that she would always come and stop me.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I turned the Lavender Melon in Konda Village into potatoes, and Sunsettias into tigers. The sneaky kitsune would normally turn up to stop me at that point, but this time was different.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: So I felt really angry afterwards and decided to go and destroy the statues of her kin. That was when I discovered the comb.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I thought to myself, "that sneaky kitsune would surely be flustered and appear if I stole this comb." So I did.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: In the end, a young human appeared instead of that sneaky kitsune. If mine mind serves me well, he was one of the three who learned their arts from the Yougou Tengu.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I had no idea why he was so strong, but he was able to seal me and the others into the stone statues.

choices.text: About your bout with the kitsune...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Terrible, isn't it? That kitsune dared to challenged me to hide-and-seek.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: She even said "Don't show yourself for anything," "If anything happens, it's me using spells to provoke you." Weird, right?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I'm a bake-danuki, as well as the Protector of the Grove. Naturally, I couldn't turn down a challenge of hide-and-seek in the Chinju Forest.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I found a great spot and turned myself into an Onikabuto, so I could watch as she ran all over the place looking for me!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: However, she never came, and so the challenge goes on.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I will keep waiting for that sneaky kitsune to come back and apologize to me. Hmph, actually, there's a lot she needs to apologize for! I'll have her know that I'm keeping score!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: The Chinju Forest used to be the territory of yours truly, Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove, and my kind, up until that human turned us into stone.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: So if you see stone statues that look like me, there's probably a bake-danuki sealed inside.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: However, the seals seem to have loosened recently. Kichiboushi and the others have returned to their original form, so there's still hope for me yet.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hey, can you promise me something?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Be nice to my little bake-danuki when you see them out there.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: They've been sealed for so long... All they want to do is see the outside world.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ah, that person would probably recite some complicated poem right now... See you around.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Come and play with me when you are free. I mean... I'm a stone after all, so I've got nothing but time to play.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Eek! I—I... Mine name is Ioroi. Do whatever you want! K—Kill me if that be your will!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, the statue is talking! And it's so scared that it can barely string a sentence together!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: I am no statue! This unseemly appearance is but the work of a temporary seal! Mine name is Ioroi, the world-renowned bake-danuki!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: What? Are you telling me that folk nowadays have heard naught of Ioroi?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: The "Tanuki Gyouen Scroll," "Ioroi's Teapot," "Kakushigami Oobayashi," "Yougou Tanuki Gassen"... Of these tales have you heard nothing?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ah, how long has mine seal persisted...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: What? You aren't here to destroy me? Come now, why did you not say so earlier, then?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: *cough* Ahem. Well then, speak! Why have you come seeking me, the lord of bake-danuki?

choices.text: This is about the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: The Sacred Secular what now? What is that? Some manner of oni treasure?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This guy is unbelievable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Is he really Miss Masked Maiden's old friend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we're looking for something hidden inside a kitsune statue.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eek... Uh, Wh—Why are you l—looking for that, might I ask?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ugh, it's on that comb's account that I was sealed in here for...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I don't know how long it's been! Sunlight doesn't come through the Chinju Forest. There's no way to tell time!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Back then, I wreaked havoc everywhere to lure that sneaky kitsune out, but it was all in vain.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eventually, I decided to vent my anger by dismantling one of those kitsune statues, and I found a comb inside... Which gave me an idea!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: The comb was hidden inside a kitsune statue and even had the Hakushin symbol on it, which reminded me of her white fur...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Thus, I concluded immediately that it must be very important. In which case, I just needed to hide the comb, and that sneaky kitsune would surely come out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, treasure's a good way to lure people out for sure! Then what happened?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Then came one of the humans from the Yougou Three. He defeated my tribe and I, turning all of us to stone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why Ioroi is afraid of humans...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmph! Humans. They're so short-lived, and they can't even transform... I don't get why that kitsune likes them so much.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: That guy who sealed me up was especially infuriating. He even told me to "strike a nice pose so that I can become nice scenery." Why, that little—!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, you do make for nice scenery...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eh? You... How could you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #(Hey, {NICKNAME}, don't annoy him, or we may never get that ward...)

choices.text: I mean to say that you look really bold and burly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! You make this dark forest look so much more colorful!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: And?

choices.text: Like the statue of a god...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, so, being sealed up is not such a bad thing after all, eh? See, humans don't mean you any harm!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I reckon I can see where you're going, but at the same time... I also... don't?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could we borrow that comb you spoke of?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Well, you certainly could... But only if you play with the children first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sure, that's easy. {NICKNAME} is good with kids!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Shousei, Gyoubu Koban, and Kichiboushi. Go find these <color=#00E1FFFF>three little tanuki</color> and play with them. I would do it, but as you can see, I'm not exactly at any liberty to move.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: That dratted fellow was a bit sloppy when he sealed them. That's why some of them were able to get out earlier.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: ...Wait, that's not correct! We should say, rather, that we bake-danuki are most powerful indeed. It's only normal, therefore, that we could free ourselves from a mere human seal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem! You speak truth, Ioroi the mighty and powerful!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Although their power can't really compare to mine, they can still use it to hide themselves.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Alright then, off you go.

choices.text: That's right, I play with Paimon all the time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

choices.text: Even the Statues of The Seven pale in comparison...
I mean that you are truly handsome and truly...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Warts? Are those edible? We bake-danuki do know quite a bit about cooking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, it's the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Victuals? Oh, it's been too long since I've had any victuals...

choices.text: I am here to collect a debt.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Uh, collect a debt? Where? When was that? Let me think, let me think...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: You, uh... What do I owe you, again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's thinking really hard...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You probably shouldn't tell this sort of joke in front of strangers.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: That's right, jest not so!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mm, it's all good, it's all good... Actually, best I make sure. Do I really owe you nothing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Do you really owe that many debts?

dialogues.speaker: Big Tanuki
dialogues.text: Go.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Hehe, well done! They seem to be quite happy.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Oh, no problem. Let me ask them for you.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Gyoubu Koban was asking, "If you are humans, why do you smell like tanuki?"

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Actually, that's right! I demand an explanation! Why *do* you smell like tanuki?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? You're only asking this now...

choices.text: It was the masked shrine maiden...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! That's what happened!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden cooked us a very lavish meal earlier, and she said that she used magic she secretly learned from the bake-danuki to make it.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: What? She learned our magic in secret? How dare she...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmm... Could it be...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Oh, come on. That sneaky kitsune! If she was still alive, she could at least have come over to say hello, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's a shrine maiden with a mask, and she called you an "old friend."

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mask? I don't know anyone with a mask. Don't know any shrine maidens, either. I sure do know a kitsune, though.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: ...That said, that sneaky kitsune did appear in the form of a shrine maiden before. What does the shrine maiden you speak of look like?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She wears a white fox mask...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Anything else?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And she wore a shrine maiden outfit.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmm... Don't know her. Never seen anyone like that in mine life!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: ...Mm? Yeah, sure, leave it to me.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Shousei said, "It was fun playing with you. Thanks!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon had a lot of fun too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, about that comb...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Now, now — I am the world renowned bake-danuki Ioroi, and I will surely keep my word. You may have the comb.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: But what do you plan to do with the comb, anyway? It probably still smells like kitsune.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, here's what happened...

choices.text: She was dressed as a shrine maiden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And she had short black hair!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: What? I didn't realize that it was so important. You should've said so earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Agh, I was sealed over this thing for...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ugh! Stop speaking so lightly of my misfortunes!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Never mind. It's all water under the bridge now. I do also have some inkling about the barrier near the forest.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Back when I was fighting that sneaky kitsune, I once saw it on the eastern seashore. It looks like a Thunder Sakura with a torii gate, right?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Back when that guy was battling the demons or whatever, I was worried that some of them might come out to hurt us. So I used magic to put a seal on that place.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Let me see. The seal should be under the cliff face to the east... Kichiboushi, take them there and remove the seal.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you, Ioroi.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Alright, alright. Enough jibber-jabber. Go now.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: If you run into that sneaky kitsune, remember to send her my regards. Just say... let me think...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: "You've ticked me off real good this time, you jerk. Come back and fight me — our contest isn't over yet! And help me break this seal while you're at it, would you? It's not as if I couldn't do it myself or anything, but you still owe me a favor! Also, Gyoubu Koban says he misses you!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, whoa, that's a lot to remember!

talks.objective: Head to the location of the barrier

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Ooh... I do so wish to scratch mine belly...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Mm? You're back already? Go on, help me find Shousei, Gyoubu Koban, and Kichiboushi, and go <color=#00E1FFFF>play with them.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Alright then, off you go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is it? It's just a bunch of bare stones...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? He seems to be using some kind of magic to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! The stones disappeared!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this is bake-danuki magic? Seems kinda fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you, Kichiboushi! Let's play Hide-and-Seek next time.

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mm!

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That was well done — whether it was dealing with Ioroi's illusory tricks, or the way you defeated those demons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Eek!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or so Paimon might have said, but this trick of yours is getting real old, Miss Masked Maiden.

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: Ah, so I disappointed you, then? I apologize. I'll do better next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no need to "do better" at trivial things like this...

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That is true. So, as for Ioroi... Is he doing well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though he's been turned into stone.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Usually, when bake-danuki make a mess, we won't send anyone to deal with them as long as they don't cross the line. After all, although they are mischievous, they're kind-hearted and simple, just like children.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: But when Ioroi dared to steal the ward for the Cleansing Ritual, well, that was enough to get him punished. Since the "Yougou Three" were mentioned in your story, then it was probably Kamuna... an onmyouji from a past age, who did the deed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked Maiden, are you Ioroi's kitsune friend?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...That's quite the compliment. He was actually talking about the daughter of the Hakushin bloodline, also known as the "Kitsune Saiguu." She was worshiped as the kitsune goddess in many places long ago.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: The Sky Kitsune and Earth Kitsune were once her emissaries. After she left, they all turned into stone statues to preserve their power and await her return — and when she does, they will all walk the Byakko Plain together once more.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Following her departure, the bloodline and mystical might of the kitsune on Narukami Island today have dwindled to less than one tenth of what they used to be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ioroi said "Our contest isn't over yet!"

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Oh, that. This is what happened. Did you know that Ioroi's full name is "Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove"?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Ioroi may be dull and impish, but he is also kind and loyal. That's why the Kitsune Saiguu aimed to guide him to the right path a long time ago.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: In order to make sure that he would comply with the Electro Archon's rule, the Kitsune Saiguu set the two of them up and got Ioroi appointed as the Protector of the Grove. This made him responsible for the safety of the Chinju Forest.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: That's why, when the world became pitch black, the Kitsune Saiguu was worried that Ioroi might die while fighting against this inexorable evil in his capacity as protector of the forest.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: So she used a game of Hide-and-Seek, something the bake-danuki are good at, as a way to challenge him...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "Ioroi, whatever happens... they're all my magical tricks. Don't fall for them and don't show up," she said.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "Of course, you sneaky kitsune. I will definitely defeat you this time," said Ioroi. And that's how their endless contest began.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So Ioroi is still waiting for her to come back and find him?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Based on what you said about Ioroi, that appears to be the case...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: But after a while, Ioroi sensed that something was wrong and started wreaking havoc. He even stole the ward in an attempt to lure the Kitsune Saiguu out.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: He didn't realize that it was something required for the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. He just thought that it was a comb of some importance to the Kitsune Saiguu. Later on, Kamuna sealed him into stone due to that misstep.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the Kitsune Saiguu, then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: ...She was swallowed up by the darkness. In the end, after that darkness was defeated, she returned to the great land of Narukami along with the soil.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And who are you then?

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Me? As you can see, I am just "Hanachirusato." A shrine maiden who wants to borrow your strength to destroy these evils.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That wasn't my question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Masked... Hanachirusato, it's really strange that you know so many things about the past that most people don't.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You even know how to use bake-danuki magic and cook tanuki dishes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But you don't know much about the present.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's almost like you're someone from a few centuries ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We also saw someone who looked like you in some memories. She even had the same name as you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You must be just like Ioroi, a bake-danuki who was sealed several centuries ago!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: N—No, that's not who I...

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I inherited her memories. As for other things, please forgive me. I cannot speak of them yet.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I made you a promise, back there in the cave. So when the time comes, I will reveal everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do we do, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, if you say so, Paimon will have some faith in Miss Masked Maiden too!

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Thank you for your understanding.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: Now, we must part here for the time being.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Goodbye.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: "We part in body alone, for our hearts drift with the clouds."

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: I will pray for your success beneath the well in Konda Village. I shall be next to the Thunder Sakura root that you cleansed successfully.

response.speaker: Hanachirusato
response.text: When the tree roots at all five places have been cleansed, please look for me there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he's very well!

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That was well done — whether it was dealing with Ioroi's illusory tricks, or the way you defeated those demons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Eek!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or so Paimon might have said, but this trick of yours is getting real old, Miss Masked Maiden.

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: Ah, so I disappointed you, then? I apologize. I'll do better next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no need to "do better" at trivial things like this...

dialogues.speaker: Hanachirusato
dialogues.text: That is true. So, as for Ioroi... Is he doing well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though he's been turned into stone.

response.text: I see...
